title: Metzgar, Stefano Secure Over $570,000 in State Funding
raw_text:
Metzgar, Stefano Secure Over $570,000 in State Funding
March 18, 2026
Funding will provide more reliable source of heat in Rockwood
HARRISBURG – Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-69) and Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32) announced they secured a grant totaling more than $570,000 for Rockwood Area School District from the Pipeline Investment Program (PIPE) for the extension of natural gas service through Rockwood Borough to the school district's facilities.
The project will install around 15,100 feet of natural gas pipeline to bring reliable gas service to the area. Currently, the school district’s heat and hot water come from a 39-year-old coal-fired boiler that is well past its useful life and requires daily maintenance to keep running. Since it burns coal and produces ash, the system also requires expensive environmental permits and ongoing regulatory fees.
By switching to natural gas, Metzgar and Stefano indicate the project will provide a more reliable source of heat for the school. It will also make natural gas available to nearby homes and businesses that are not currently connected, including ASSA ABLOY, a security door manufacturer, as well as Rockwood Casualty Insurance, the local fire department and seven other businesses.
“Reliable heat is not a luxury. It is a necessity for our schools and community,” said Metzgar. “This is a massive win for Rockwood as this funding will obtain a more dependable heating source that lowers long-term costs and ensures students and staff can learn and work in a safe, comfortable environment.”
“I know that for Rockwood, this investment feels like a weight being lifted. The school district will be relieved of the constant worry that came with keeping the old system running,” Stefano said. “I’m proud to see that with this funding, the school and the families and the businesses that surround it can look toward a future with dependable, modern energy service. It’s a win for the classroom, as well as the entire community.”
PIPE provides grants to construct the last few miles of natural gas distribution lines to business parks, existing manufacturing and industrial enterprises, which will result in the creation of new economic base jobs in the Commonwealth while providing access to natural gas for residents. Funds may be used for acquisition, construction and site preparation costs associated with extending natural gas pipelines to serve eligible applicants.

title: Metzgar, Stefano Raise Concern Over Faulty Work in Somerset Lake’s Rehabilitation
raw_text:
Metzgar, Stefano Raise Concern Over Faulty Work in Somerset Lake’s Rehabilitation
March 13, 2026
HARRISBURG
– Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-69) and Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32) released a joint statement regarding the continuous structural issues following a restoration project at Somerset Lake:
“After meeting with the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission (PFBC), we were informed, yet again, that Somerset Lake’s dam has ended up in need of repair. It was communicated to us that, amid the project, the contractor made changes to the project specifications that the engineer did not identify or correct. Even more troubling, this happened under the watch of the governor’s Department of General Services (DGS), the agency that was ultimately responsible for overseeing the entire project.
“While the project was technically completed, this communication breakdown has led to brand new structural problems long before we should see any wear and tear of the dam. It’s hard to believe these avoidable mistakes were permitted, derailing the progress already made.
“This situation reinforces, in the strongest possible terms, the need for clear communication, accountability and transparency throughout every stage of publicly funded work. Our constituents deserve confidence that restoration projects at our lakes are handled with the utmost care and accuracy for the best interest in their safety. Those basic expectations were clearly not met here.
“As the bondholder, DGS must take corrective action to address the problems at Somerset Lake.  Additionally, as PFBC and DGS continue preparations for repairs at neighboring High Point Lake, it is vital that these agencies learn their lesson regarding this structural design and who they award contracts to for these projects. They must pause any development and review what went wrong at Somerset Lake to ensure we don’t face the same preventable errors.
“Our priority remains ensuring any publicly funded projects are done safely and without further disruption to the people of Somerset County.”

title: Metzgar to Introduce Legislation to Eliminate Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission’s Use of Eminent Domain
raw_text:
Metzgar to Introduce Legislation to Eliminate Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission’s Use of Eminent Domain
February 6, 2026
HARRISBURG
– To reign in the overreach of the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission (PTC), Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-Somerset) announced his intention to introduce legislation that would eliminate the entity’s ability to exercise the power of eminent domain – citing growing concerns over reckless expansion plans that threaten private property rights and Pennsylvania’s natural heritage.
In 2024, the PTC revealed that, despite repeated opposition by the public, it was entering into a four-year preliminary engineering stage for a project that would put a 1,000-foot cut through the Allegheny Mountain near the existing Turnpike tunnels.
This maneuver would seize private property and cause significant disruptions to surrounding ecosystems, local climate conditions and nearby communities, leading to irreversible damage to the environment and quality of life. According to Metzgar, those who rely on the mountain for water supply through wells and natural springs – including Berlin Borough – could face immense danger because of contamination and scarcity.
Given the mitigating risk factors and PTC’s relentless pursuit of this project, Metzgar said urgent action is required to restore balance and protect Pennsylvanians from government overreach.
“Taking away eminent domain would re-establish a landowner’s ability to consent,” said Metzgar. “It is my understanding the landowners do not consent to having their land taken, nor to put this enormous cut through the mountain. My plan is the best course of action to deter the Turnpike Commission’s egregious behavior and put the people first.”

Metzgar to Introduce Legislation to Give Pennsylvania Sportsmen a Voice on Deer Season Opening Day
September 30, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-Somerset) announced today he is preparing to introduce legislation that would give Pennsylvania hunters and trappers more say in decisions impacting hunting seasons and traditions in the Commonwealth.
Metzgar’s proposal would require the Pennsylvania Game Commission (PGC) to conduct a brief, optional survey when residents purchase their annual hunting or trapping license. The key question would ask hunters when the statewide firearms deer season should begin. If participants decide to take part, they must choose one of the following options: current Saturday after Thanksgiving or return to the traditional Monday after Thanksgiving.
The results of the survey would carry significant weight instead of being seen as a symbolic gesture. According to Metzgar, PGC would be tasked with amending regulations to reflect the will of those who cast their votes. Any changes made would be in effect for 10 years. Resident hunting license applicants would vote in the ninth year to set the opening day for the next 10-year period, ensuring a smooth transition and preventing implementation hiccups.
“Pennsylvania’s hunters and trappers deserve a meaningful voice in this process because they are directly impacted by the Game Commission’s decisions,” said Metzgar. “My intent is to create a direct, data-driven pathway for participants to disclose their preferences in a meaningful way.”

Metzgar to Introduce Legislation to Give Pennsylvania Sportsmen a Voice on Deer Season Opening Day
September 30, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-Somerset) announced today he is preparing to introduce legislation that would give Pennsylvania hunters and trappers more say in decisions impacting hunting seasons and traditions in the Commonwealth.
Metzgar’s proposal would require the Pennsylvania Game Commission (PGC) to conduct a brief, optional survey when residents purchase their annual hunting or trapping license. The key question would ask hunters when the statewide firearms deer season should begin. If participants decide to take part, they must choose one of the following options: current Saturday after Thanksgiving or return to the traditional Monday after Thanksgiving.
The results of the survey would carry significant weight instead of being seen as a symbolic gesture. According to Metzgar, PGC would be tasked with amending regulations to reflect the will of those who cast their votes. Any changes made would be in effect for 10 years. Resident hunting license applicants would vote in the ninth year to set the opening day for the next 10-year period, ensuring a smooth transition and preventing implementation hiccups.
“Pennsylvania’s hunters and trappers deserve a meaningful voice in this process because they are directly impacted by the Game Commission’s decisions,” said Metzgar. “My intent is to create a direct, data-driven pathway for participants to disclose their preferences in a meaningful way.”

Metzgar, Stefano Secure Over $570,000 in State Funding
March 18, 2026
Funding will provide more reliable source of heat in Rockwood
HARRISBURG – Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-69) and Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32) announced they secured a grant totaling more than $570,000 for Rockwood Area School District from the Pipeline Investment Program (PIPE) for the extension of natural gas service through Rockwood Borough to the school district's facilities.
The project will install around 15,100 feet of natural gas pipeline to bring reliable gas service to the area. Currently, the school district’s heat and hot water come from a 39-year-old coal-fired boiler that is well past its useful life and requires daily maintenance to keep running. Since it burns coal and produces ash, the system also requires expensive environmental permits and ongoing regulatory fees.
By switching to natural gas, Metzgar and Stefano indicate the project will provide a more reliable source of heat for the school. It will also make natural gas available to nearby homes and businesses that are not currently connected, including ASSA ABLOY, a security door manufacturer, as well as Rockwood Casualty Insurance, the local fire department and seven other businesses.
“Reliable heat is not a luxury. It is a necessity for our schools and community,” said Metzgar. “This is a massive win for Rockwood as this funding will obtain a more dependable heating source that lowers long-term costs and ensures students and staff can learn and work in a safe, comfortable environment.”
“I know that for Rockwood, this investment feels like a weight being lifted. The school district will be relieved of the constant worry that came with keeping the old system running,” Stefano said. “I’m proud to see that with this funding, the school and the families and the businesses that surround it can look toward a future with dependable, modern energy service. It’s a win for the classroom, as well as the entire community.”
PIPE provides grants to construct the last few miles of natural gas distribution lines to business parks, existing manufacturing and industrial enterprises, which will result in the creation of new economic base jobs in the Commonwealth while providing access to natural gas for residents. Funds may be used for acquisition, construction and site preparation costs associated with extending natural gas pipelines to serve eligible applicants.

Metzgar, Stefano Raise Concern Over Faulty Work in Somerset Lake’s Rehabilitation
March 13, 2026
HARRISBURG
– Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-69) and Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32) released a joint statement regarding the continuous structural issues following a restoration project at Somerset Lake:
“After meeting with the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission (PFBC), we were informed, yet again, that Somerset Lake’s dam has ended up in need of repair. It was communicated to us that, amid the project, the contractor made changes to the project specifications that the engineer did not identify or correct. Even more troubling, this happened under the watch of the governor’s Department of General Services (DGS), the agency that was ultimately responsible for overseeing the entire project.
“While the project was technically completed, this communication breakdown has led to brand new structural problems long before we should see any wear and tear of the dam. It’s hard to believe these avoidable mistakes were permitted, derailing the progress already made.
“This situation reinforces, in the strongest possible terms, the need for clear communication, accountability and transparency throughout every stage of publicly funded work. Our constituents deserve confidence that restoration projects at our lakes are handled with the utmost care and accuracy for the best interest in their safety. Those basic expectations were clearly not met here.
“As the bondholder, DGS must take corrective action to address the problems at Somerset Lake.  Additionally, as PFBC and DGS continue preparations for repairs at neighboring High Point Lake, it is vital that these agencies learn their lesson regarding this structural design and who they award contracts to for these projects. They must pause any development and review what went wrong at Somerset Lake to ensure we don’t face the same preventable errors.
“Our priority remains ensuring any publicly funded projects are done safely and without further disruption to the people of Somerset County.”

Metzgar to Introduce Legislation to Eliminate Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission’s Use of Eminent Domain
February 6, 2026
HARRISBURG
– To reign in the overreach of the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission (PTC), Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-Somerset) announced his intention to introduce legislation that would eliminate the entity’s ability to exercise the power of eminent domain – citing growing concerns over reckless expansion plans that threaten private property rights and Pennsylvania’s natural heritage.
In 2024, the PTC revealed that, despite repeated opposition by the public, it was entering into a four-year preliminary engineering stage for a project that would put a 1,000-foot cut through the Allegheny Mountain near the existing Turnpike tunnels.
This maneuver would seize private property and cause significant disruptions to surrounding ecosystems, local climate conditions and nearby communities, leading to irreversible damage to the environment and quality of life. According to Metzgar, those who rely on the mountain for water supply through wells and natural springs – including Berlin Borough – could face immense danger because of contamination and scarcity.
Given the mitigating risk factors and PTC’s relentless pursuit of this project, Metzgar said urgent action is required to restore balance and protect Pennsylvanians from government overreach.
“Taking away eminent domain would re-establish a landowner’s ability to consent,” said Metzgar. “It is my understanding the landowners do not consent to having their land taken, nor to put this enormous cut through the mountain. My plan is the best course of action to deter the Turnpike Commission’s egregious behavior and put the people first.”

PFC Gilbert’s legacy will live forever in Somerset County and Washington, D.C. In the nation’s capital, his name is displayed on Panel 5E, Line 50 on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial.

title: Metzgar Secures Crucial Commitment from DCNR
raw_text:
Metzgar Secures Crucial Commitment from DCNR
March 25, 2025
Agency to spray for spring moths and fall cankerworms
HARRISBURG – Witnessing the widespread defoliation caused by fall cankerworms and spring moths in the beautiful Somerset County area over the last two to three years, and after extensive discussions with the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR), Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-Somerset) announced the agency has committed to spraying for these pests. Metzgar notes this is a win for the area, as DCNR has recognized the urgency of the issue.
“As warmer temperatures approach, it is crucial for forest landowners and woodlot owners to start considering aerial treatments to protect trees from the devastating effects of Lymantria dispar dispar (spring moths) and fall cankerworms,” said Metzgar. “These pests pose a significant threat to our forests, having already destroyed millions of trees.”
In response to this crisis, Metzgar has championed the effort to create a comprehensive plan to assist landowners. This includes lining up a list of trusted aerial applicators, providing a suppression guide, and coordinating with expert foresters to help landowners with the planning and treatment process.
Key Information for Landowners:
•
Eggs
: Be on the lookout for the light tan eggs laid by female moths between June and July. These eggs can contain between 100 to 1,500 individual eggs and are typically found on trees, rocks and other surfaces.
•
Treatment Window
: The critical period for treatment is during the small caterpillar stage in May. This is when treatment is most effective.
•
Recommended Treatments
: Bacillus thuringiensis kurstaki (Btk) and Tebufenozide (Mimic) are the most commonly used treatments for these pests.
•
Urgency:
Due to a limited number of applicators and a narrow treatment window, it's important to schedule services as soon as possible.

Founded in 1988, PENNVEST provides grants and low-interest loans for design, engineering and construction of publicly and privately owned drinking water distribution and treatment facilities, as well as storm water and wastewater projects. For more information on the PENNVEST program, visit

title: Metzgar, Stefano to Host Veterans Appreciation Breakfast Nov. 12
raw_text:
Metzgar, Stefano to Host Veterans Appreciation Breakfast Nov. 12
October 27, 2026
SOMERSET – To show appreciation for those who served the country, Rep. Carl Walker Metzgar (R-69) and Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32) will host a free breakfast for veterans on Thursday, Nov. 12, at the Somerset American Legion Post 181, 162 W. Main St. in Somerset.
The event begins with registration at 8:30 a.m. and breakfast will be served at 9 a.m. Somerset County veterans will be able to connect with other local veterans and learn about the services the senator’s and representative’s offices can offer for state-level assistance.
“Our veterans have given so much in service to our nation, and the least we can do is give back to those who have sacrificed for our freedoms,” said Metzgar. “Hosting this free breakfast is a small but meaningful way to express our gratitude, honor their service and remind them that their dedication and sacrifices will never be forgotten.”
“Our veterans have carried the weight of service with honor, giving more than most of us will ever fully understand,” said Stefano.  “Their service and sacrifices safeguard the freedoms we enjoy every day, and this free breakfast is a small token of our appreciation.”
Those planning to attend must register by calling Stefano’s office at 814-443-2053 or Metzgar’s office at 814-443-4230.
